measured_rates.method: delta_pct = sum over families of (input + cache_write + 5x output) x rate, plus a cache-read column, by non-negative least squares over every clean stretch of the account and side of 2026-09-14, with the Opus coefficient rescaled afterwards to 0.6667 credits per token so the fit reads in credits. Intervals are 80% bootstrap intervals over resampled stretches. A family's rate is the median of the per-fit point estimates and the union of their intervals, and only where every fit's interval for it overlaps every other's; where they do not it keeps the interval and no value.

fable.why: the fits do not agree within their intervals (a3/post 1.927x Opus [1.769, 2.803], a2/post 3.962x Opus [3.296, 4.553], a2/pre 1.960x Opus [1.854, 2.151]), so the interval is the claim and there is no single rate. The data cannot say whether Fable's rate moved or the five-hour window did: the window fitted on the same stretches moves the same way.

window_credits.method: median credits per 1% of the five-hour meter over the pure-opus stretches of every watched account's passive stretch file, times 100. A stretch counts when it moved the meter at least 3%, carries tokens, does not overlap one of the tracker's own runs on its own account (a probe row or the effort-matrix run), and reads capture_status 'accepted'. Every token in a pure-opus stretch is priced at a rate data/prices.json publishes, so the figure carries no fitted parameter. Cache writes at the input rate, cache reads at 0 of it.

window_credits_from_weekly.method: the announced weekly cap -- the January baseline times the multiplier in force (x1.5 from May, x1.25 from 14 September) -- divided by this tracker's own measured windows per week for the regime either side of the certified change. It shares no input with window_credits, which is why it is a cross-check.

window_tokens.method: median over the pure-opus clean stretches of the tokens the stretch carried per 1% of the five-hour meter, times 100, taken per token class and over all four classes together. The interval is the spread of the readings themselves -- per account its own lowest and highest per-stretch value, pooled the union of the account intervals -- and not a confidence interval. No credit rate and no class weight enters the pure-opus figure: it is the stretch's own token counts over its own meter movement. Every other family is a conversion of it at the two families' rates (`conversion`), and a family whose rate is a status sentence publishes no number.

fable.conversion: the Opus window tokens times the Opus input rate over the Fable input-rate envelope, at the same token-class mix (`per_class` above, cache reads at the published cache-read weight); the interval combines the window interval with the rate interval. The envelope has no single rate, so there is no value, only the interval.

sonnet.conversion: the Opus window tokens times the Opus input rate over the measured Sonnet input rate, at the same token-class mix (`per_class` above, cache reads at the published cache-read weight); the interval combines the window interval with the rate interval.

all.status: not measurable, no clean stretch is Haiku-heavy

window_tokens.selection: A stretch counts when it moved the meter at least 3%, carries tokens, does not overlap one of the tracker's own runs on its own account (a probe row or the effort-matrix run), and reads capture_status 'accepted'.
